upstream.inspection: Official GPUI README describes a Rust GPU-accelerated framework with native Windows support. gpuix describes Node.js/Bun bindings for React or Solid. Use GPUI directly for the requested Rust GUI; gpuix may inform reference work but is not selected as the final runtime.
upstream.macosTextBackend: The desktop GUI must enable gpui_platform/font-kit, which forwards to gpui_macos/font-kit and the pinned gpui_apple text backend. NoopTextSystem is not a valid shipping desktop text renderer. Enabling the existing feature must preserve the locked dependency revisions; actual readable text and native input require macOS desktop verification.
upstream.versionDecision: Workspace pins zed-industries/zed revision b0f1e1cb2f4be4c7df054f96a2a2721aa878ba6c for GPUI and gpui_platform. Maintained crates under rust/vendor use that same revision: gpui_wgpu, gpui_windows and gpui_apple fix tile-local texture sampling; gpui, gpui_linux, gpui_macos and gpui_windows carry native export-drag lifecycle support. Windows embeds HLSL sources and uses the existing D3D compiler when creating renderer shaders, removing host-Windows SDK and build-directory requirements in both profiles at the cost of release startup compilation. Inherited dependency versions and features remain unchanged; the obsolete Windows SDK lookup build dependency is removed. Successful platform builds and executable GUI workflow verification remain required.

clipboardImport.requirement: GPUI reads real OS clipboard image entries and sends encoded bytes to the same Rust decoder/document source admission as file loading. Path and clipboard origins remain explicit; no temporary source files or fictional recent-file entries.
clipboardImport.presentation: Expose Paste image and Ctrl/Cmd+V outside text fields. Text fields consume paste as text, including image-only clipboard contents. Refuse import during active jobs, batch mode or another modal; confirm replacement of segmentation edits. Failed or cancelled admission retains the current document.
clipboardImport.namingEvidence: source-entry-contract.json records the static native clipboard handler assigning clipboard.png in the current source directory and the display title [From clipboard]. source-history-reference.ndjson.gz covers real-path history only; retained gui/source-controller.mjs records only successful disk loads. Use clipboard.png solely as an export suggestion, never as a readable source or recent file.
clipboardImport.limits: Original Windows clipboard acquisition, exact clipboard alpha conversion, clipboard preview scaling and after-answer replacement behavior remain unverified. The GPUI import requires separate live platform proof; this requirement is not a native parity claim.

sourceFileProtection.requirement: CLI vectorize and GPUI save admission must reject an output identifying its file-backed source, including direct paths, symlinks and hardlinks, before overwrite confirmation or writing, even when CLI --force is supplied. Both use the shared Rust filesystem-identity helper, not only canonical or case-folded paths. Unix identity checks must use metadata without opening file contents or requiring read permission on a writable destination. Distinct case-sensitive filenames remain distinct. Clipboard names are not file identities. A different output remains saveable after rejection.
sourceFileProtection.evidence: The disposable-image workflow in evidence/gpui-save-aliases-20261021/check.py exposed source truncation through a confirmed hardlink save and rejection of a write-only destination. evidence/cli-source-aliases-20261021/check.py exposed symlink/hardlink source truncation under --force and false rejection of a distinct case-sensitive filename. This is an application safety requirement, not a claim about the original application's behavior.

dragResult.nativeEvidence: window-reset-contract.json records two DragResultWidget owners, AI/DXF/EMF/EPS/PDF/SVG choices, AI default and Minimize on drag enabled.
dragResult.implementation: Prepare exports through the shared Rust engine and hand real files to the OS using copy-only native drag/drop. Distinguish rejection before native acceptance, platform start, accepted drop, cancellation and failure. Minimize only after native ownership is established. Keep the active file alive throughout handoff; retain it on native start or completion of an accepted attempt, including cancellation/failure, because a destination may read it later. Rejected startup does not retain a never-offered file, and cannot undo retention from an earlier accepted attempt. Recheck current source/geometry, export options and workflow state at gesture admission and native handoff; stale preparation and cancellation must not expose partial or unrelated files.
dragResult.limits: Native drop effects, precise minimize/restore timing and export-file lifetime have not been captured. Platform implementations and actual receiver workflows require verification; these implementation requirements do not establish native parity.

windowsExecutable.requirement: Windows release GUI executables use the Windows GUI subsystem so normal desktop launch does not create a console window. Debug builds retain console diagnostics. CLI binaries retain their console subsystem.
windowsExecutable.verification: Inspect the packaged PE subsystem and exercise the exact package executable on the authorized Windows test host. A cross-build alone does not prove runtime behavior.
